headline: Subscription growth lifts margins; FY guidance raised
summary_short: MSCI grew Q2 FY2026 revenue 12.2% y/y to $867.0M and diluted EPS 19.6% y/y to $4.69, then raised its full-year 2026 operating-expense, interest, D&A and free-cash-flow guidance.
summary_long: Revenue rose 12.2% y/y to $867.0M (also 12.2% organic), driven by $50.6M higher subscription revenue and $49.0M higher asset-based fees on record index-linked ETF AUM; Index segment revenue grew 17.5%. Operating margin expanded to 56.2% from 55.0% as opex growth (+9.2%) trailed revenue growth. Diluted EPS was $4.69 (+19.6% y/y); adjusted EPS was $4.94 (+18.5% y/y). Free cash flow rose 8.2% to $326.4M; MSCI repurchased $145.0M of stock and paid $149.2M in dividends, leaving cash of $356.4M against $6.4B debt and a $2,689.5M shareholders' deficit. MSCI raised FY2026 opex, EBITDA-expense, interest, D&A, operating-cash-flow and free-cash-flow guidance, citing the pending First Street acquisition and stronger topline momentum.

drivers.explanation: Recurring subscription revenue rose $50.6M and asset-based fees rose $49.0M on record ETF AUM linked to MSCI indexes, partially offset by $5.3M lower non-recurring revenue; Index segment led with 17.5% growth.

Total operating expenses rose 9.2% against 12.2% revenue growth, reflecting higher IT, market-data, professional-fee and headcount costs, partially offset by operating leverage on the larger recurring-subscription base.

Higher operating income was partly offset by a 47.8% rise in other expense, net, from higher interest expense on increased debt levels, while the effective tax rate fell to 18.0% from 19.6% on US tax law changes and earnings mix.

EPS benefited from net income growth plus a 5.9% y/y reduction in weighted diluted shares from buybacks; the q/q decline reflects a Q1 2026 base that included a one-off tax benefit, not a Q2 shortfall.

CEO Henry Fernandez cited a 'record asset-based-fee run rate' and 'accelerated run-rate growth' in Index and Private Capital Solutions, plus record hedge-fund and asset-owner net-new sales; guidance was raised partly reflecting the pending First Street acquisition.
